title: Quasi-compact quasi-separated zero-dimensional schemes are affine
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] that is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Suppose every point of $X$ is closed (equivalently, $X$ has topological Krull dimension at most zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]). Then $X$ is affine: there is a commutative ring $A$ and an isomorphism $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$. The empty scheme is allowed. No Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero: implication (1) to (2) and final assertion that a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme of dimension zero is affine.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-t1-finite-hausdorff-affine-cover] to $X$, using the given quasi-compactness and closedness of every point. Obtain a finite affine open covering $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ with each $U_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ quasi-compact and Hausdorff. This includes the empty scheme with an empty cover.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, opening proof paragraph: affine charts are profinite, and final paragraph: choose a finite affine open covering of a quasi-compact open. The closed-point formulation makes explicit the maximal-prime argument in the returned item, old steps 1, 2 and the chart-topology part of step 3.

proof.text: Use the Hausdorff affine covering from step 1 in [lem-sfb-hausdorff-charts-qc-open-closed]. Its quasi-separatedness hypothesis is the given one on $X$. Each $U_i$ is a quasi-compact open by step 1, so its original inclusion $U_i\hookrightarrow X$ is a closed immersion. Thus the same finite family consists of affine closed subschemes and still covers $X$ set theoretically.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, proof of (1) implies (2): quasi-compact overlaps are closed in Hausdorff affine charts, and an open immersion with closed image is closed. Local closedness generalized to any quasi-compact open, with the finite-neighbourhood argument and local-to-global complement calculation of the returned item, old steps 3 (overlaps), 4 and 5.

proof.text: The finitely many affine closed subschemes $U_i\hookrightarrow X$ of step 2 cover $X$ set theoretically by step 1. Apply [lem-sc-closed-affine-union-affine] to this family: $X$ is affine, so there exist a commutative ring $A$ and an isomorphism $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its statement explicitly includes the empty family for $X=\varnothing$. This uses neither a Noetherian nor a finite-type hypothesis. It completes the finite-cover argument using the existing general closed-cover affineness lemma.
